questions.question: Which of the following was the unique feature of Dholavira’s city layout during the Indus Valley Civilisation?

options.text: It was a single unique tomb.
It was divided into two distinct parts.
It was divided into eight parts.
It was divided into three distinct parts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It was divided into three distinct parts.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dholavira, one of the prominent cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation, had a unique layout divided into **three distinct parts**—the citadel, the middle town, and the lower town.
 
• Each part was meticulously planned and fortified with massive walls made of stone and bricks, showcasing advanced urban engineering.
 
• The city also featured an innovative water conservation system, including reservoirs, step wells, and stormwater channels, highlighting its adaptation to arid conditions.
 
• Dholavira is located in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, India, and is considered one of the most significant archaeological sites of the Harappan period.
 
• The distinctive three-part division reflects Dholavira's socio-political organization and planning excellence during the Harappan era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilisation:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilisation, also known as the Harappan Civilisation, flourished between 2600 BCE and 1900 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It is renowned for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and drainage systems.
 
• Major cities of the civilisation include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Significance of Dholavira:**
 
 
• Dholavira was discovered in 1967-68 by archaeologist Jagat Pati Joshi.
 
• The site provides insights into Harappan urban planning, water management, and socio-economic structures.
 
• UNESCO recognized Dholavira as a **World Heritage Site** in 2021.
 
 
 
• **Water Management in Dholavira:**
 
 
• Dholavira's water management system included large reservoirs and interconnected channels.
 
• This system was designed to store rainwater and manage seasonal water scarcity effectively.
 
 
 
• **Socio-political Structure of Dholavira:**
 
 
• The division into three parts suggests a hierarchical social structure, with the citadel likely housing the ruling elite.
 
• The middle and lower towns accommodated artisans, traders, and common citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following Indus Valley sites was discovered by Rakhal Das Bannerjee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-Daro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is one of the most significant sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• It was discovered in **1922** by the Indian archaeologist **Rakhal Das Bannerjee**.
 
• The site is known for its advanced urban planning, including a well-organized grid layout, drainage systems, and water storage facilities.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is home to iconic structures such as the **Great Bath**, which reflects the significance of ritualistic and communal activities in the civilization.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered one of the earliest examples of urbanization in human history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC):**

 
 
• It is one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, flourishing from approximately 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
 
• Prominent sites include Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, Kalibangan, Lothal, and Dholavira.
 
• The civilization is noted for its advanced town planning, standardized weights and measures, and trade practices.
 
 
 
• **Rakhal Das Bannerjee:**
 
 
• He was an Indian archaeologist and historian credited with the discovery of Mohenjo-Daro in 1922.
 
• He played a vital role in identifying the significance of the site as part of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Great Bath:**
 
 
• Located in Mohenjo-Daro, it is one of the earliest public water tanks in the world.
 
• Its construction suggests advanced engineering skills and the importance of water in rituals.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
 
• The site faces challenges such as erosion, salinity, and improper restoration techniques, necessitating conservation efforts.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not related to Kalibangan civilization?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tools of iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kalibangan civilization is part of the Indus Valley Civilization, which dates back to the Bronze Age and predates the Iron Age.
 
• Tools of iron were not discovered at Kalibangan since iron was not used during the Indus Valley period.
 
• The main materials used for tools and artifacts in Kalibangan included copper, bronze, and stone.
 
• Kalibangan is known for its unique features such as fire altars, mud-brick houses, and advanced fortifications, which were characteristic of the Harappan culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalibangan Civilization:**

 
 
• Kalibangan, located in Rajasthan, India, is an important archaeological site of the Harappan civilization.
 
• It is known for its distinctive fire altars, which suggest ritualistic practices.
 
• The site revealed evidence of both pre-Harappan (early Harappan) and mature Harappan phases.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Indus Valley Civilization:**
 
 
• Advanced town planning with grid-like layouts, drainage systems, and fortified structures.
 
• Use of mud bricks and baked bricks for construction.
 
• Artifacts include seals, pottery, beads, and tools made of copper, bronze, and stone.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age:**
 
 
• The Iron Age followed the Bronze Age and marked the use of iron for tools and weapons.
 
• It began around 1200 BCE in various parts of the world but was not part of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Fire Altars:**
 
 
• Fire altars at Kalibangan indicate ritualistic practices and the prominence of religious activities in Harappan culture.
 
• These altars are rectangular structures with evidence of ash and fire residues.

questions.question: Which among the following materials was used in making the Harappan seals ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steatite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harappan seals were predominantly made using **steatite**, a soft stone that could be easily carved and shaped into intricate designs.
 
• Steatite was often hardened by firing it in kilns, which gave the seals durability and a characteristic smooth surface.
 
• These seals typically featured inscriptions in the **Indus script** and depictions of animals such as bulls, elephants, and unicorns.
 
• The seals were likely used for administrative purposes, such as trade authentication, and as amulets or personal identifiers.
 
• Excavations at Harappan sites like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa have unearthed thousands of steatite seals, showcasing the sophistication of their craftsmanship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steatite:** Also known as soapstone, it is a metamorphic rock rich in talc, making it soft and easy to carve.
 
• **Indus Script:** The inscriptions on Harappan seals are in a script that remains undeciphered to this day, consisting of pictographic and symbolic characters.
 
• **Uses of Seals:** In addition to trade, seals may have had religious or symbolic significance, possibly representing ownership or status.
 
• **Firing Process:** The practice of firing steatite seals to harden them highlights the advanced technological knowledge of the Harappan civilization.
 
• **Animal Motifs:** The depiction of animals on the seals reflects the cultural and symbolic importance of fauna in Harappan society.

questions.question: Which Harappan site shows evidence of ploughed fields?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalibangan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kalibangan** is a prominent Harappan site located in present-day Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is unique among Harappan sites for providing evidence of **ploughed agricultural fields**.
 
• The ploughed field marks at Kalibangan are indicative of early agricultural practices in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• These field impressions were discovered near the southern part of the site, showing **furrows aligned in two directions**, suggesting advanced farming techniques.
 
• The discovery highlights the significance of agriculture in the economy of the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**:

 
 
• It is one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, dating back to** 2500 BCE**.
 
• Major sites include **Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, and Kalibangan**.
 
• Known for advanced town planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan’s Historical Significance**:
 
 
• Kalibangan is divided into two parts: the **citadel **(western mound) and the **lower town** (eastern mound).
 
• The site shows evidence of fire altars, indicating ritualistic practices.
 
• It also provides evidence of mud-brick structures typical of Harappan architecture.
 
 
 
• **Ploughed Fields in Archaeology**:
 
 
• Ploughed field impressions are rare in archaeology and provide insights into ancient agricultural practices.
 
• Such discoveries help reconstruct the methods of crop cultivation used by early civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in the Harappan Civilization**:
 
 
• Major crops included **wheat, barley, sesame, mustard, and cotton**.
 
• Advanced irrigation techniques and seasonal cultivation were practiced.
 
• Kalibangan’s evidence of ploughed fields complements the broader understanding of Harappan agriculture.

questions.question: Eastern boundary of the Harappa culture is indicated by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alamgirpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The history of India begins with the birth of the Indus Valley Civilization (IVC), also known as the Harappan Civilization. 

 
 
• It flourished around 2,500 BC, in the western part of South Asia, in contemporary Pakistan and Western India.
 
• The Indus Valley was home to the largest of the four ancient urban civilizations of **Egypt, Mesopotamia, India and China**.
 
• In the 1920s, the Archaeological Department of India carried out excavations in the Indus valley wherein the ruins of the two old cities, viz. Mohenjodaro and Harappa were unearthed.
 
• The early Harappan communities were turned into large urban centres, like Harappa and Mohenjodaro in Pakistan and Lothal in India.
 
• **Suktagendor is the westernmost **boundary of the IVC. It is located in the** Balochistan Province of Pakistan**.
 
• While** Alamgirpur is the easternmost** boundary of the IVC. This site is located in the **Meerut District of Uttar Pradesh**. **Hence option 3 is Correct**.
 
• Daimabad is the **Southermost** boundary of the IVC which is located on the **Pravara river** in the Maharshtra state.
 
• **Manda is the Northermost** boundary which is located in the present Jammu and Kashmir region on **Chenab river**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**__ Nevasa __

__
 
• **Nevasa is a city in Nevasa tehsil of Ahmednagar district in the Indian state of Maharashtra.**
 
• The remains of a multilevel settlement dating from the Palaeolithic period to the Middle Ages have been discovered at Navasa.
 
• Excavations were conducted by** H. D. Sankalia in the 1950s **and by G. Karve-Corvinus in 1967.
 
• **Nevasa's Aeneolithic layer** reveals a settled agricultural culture characterized in the second millennium B.C. by implements (elongated plates) similar to those of the Harappa civilization.

**Isampur**__

__
 
• **Isampur is an Acheulian Lower Palaeolithic site in northern Karnataka**, India.
 
• Surface surveys and excavations at the site during the last five years (1997-2001) have generated crucial data on the Indian subcontinent's Pleistocene hominid record.
 
• Isampur is the location of the country's earliest "true quarry-cum-manufacturing centre" of the Lower Palaeolithic.
 
• Over 15,000 objects, including limestone cores and debitage, as well as a variety of hammerstones, have been found from the site.

**Didwana**__

 
• There is no compiled history of Didwana, but the excavation done here has shown that this is a lower Paleolithic culture site so the activities of one of the earliest ancestors of mankind have taken place here.
 
• **It is located in Rajasthan.**
 
• Two sandy mounds 700 meters wide and 300 meters wide have been witness to human development in the flow of Bangal Canal near the city.
 
• Geophysicist Prof. V.N. of Deccan College, Pune. Mishra and SN Rajguru excavated here in the 1980s. He found around 1300 artifacts including small tools, large cutting tools such as chaperos, polyhandros, sparoids.
 
• His radio dating age is estimated at 7 lakh 97 thousand years. The Archaeological Survey of India has named these mounds 16R. The Archaeological Survey of India will conserve these earthen mounds for the first time in its history. 

**Gudiyam cave**

 
• Gudiyam Caves are rock shelters in South India and known for prehistoric stone tools and culture.
 
• They were first identified by British geologist Robert Bruce Foote. This ancient site is situated in the Thiruvallur district near the** Poondi reservoir, 60 km (37.3 mi) from Chennai, Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Archaeological evidence suggests that the caves were used by Palaeolithic Man. The site has been excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India in 1963 and 1964.
 
• Systematic palaeolithic studies in this region indicate these sites suggest extensive movement of early hominids across the landscape about 200,000 years ago.
 
• Sixteen such shelters have been identified by the Archaeological Survey of India in Allikulli Hill ranges near Poondi.

questions.question: Which animal was not known to the Indus people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Lion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, located in the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The people of this civilization were known for their advanced urban planning, sophisticated craftsmanship, and strong organizational skills.
 
• They domesticated and used various animals for different purposes. These animals included sheep, goat, humped and humpless bull, buffalo, boar, dog, cat, pig, fowl, deer, tortoise, elephants, camel, rhinoceros, and tiger.
 
• However, there is no archaeological evidence to suggest that the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the lion. This could be due to various reasons such as the lion not being native to the areas where this civilization flourished, or the lion not being a significant part of their culture or economy.

**Therefore, based on current archaeological findings and historical records, it is accurate to say that the lion was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important Features of Indus Valley Civilization**.

 
 
• ​The grid system of town Planning.
 
• Citadel ( for administrative and religious purposes) and lower town ( residence of common people).
 
• large-scale use of burnt bricks and the absence of stone buildings.
 
• Houses had many rooms with a square courtyard, private wells, kitchens, and bathing space.
 
• Well laid out underground drainage system.
